summary: This document retires the use of GOST R 34.10-2001 (ECC-GOST) and GOST R 34.11-94 in DNSSEC. It updates RFC 5933, which is historic.

plainLanguage.summary: An old Russian-standard algorithm for signing DNS records is being retired because it is no longer used.

questions: why was gost removed from dnssec
subtitle: Removes support for deprecated GOST algorithms from DNSSEC.

tldr.problem: RFC 5933 introduced two Russian-standard cryptographic algorithms (GOST R 34.10-2001 and GOST R 34.11-94) for DNSSEC, but these were officially deprecated by Russia in 2012 and have no real-world deployment in DNSSEC.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 9906 marks these algorithms as DEPRECATED in the IANA registries and mandates that DNSSEC implementations must not use them for signing or validation, and must treat records using them as insecure.
tldr.outcome: DNSSEC validators no longer recognize ECC-GOST signatures, and zone operators are discouraged from using these obsolete algorithms, improving the overall security posture of DNSSEC.

today: RFC 9906 marks these algorithms as deprecated and forbidden in DNSSEC. No new signatures should use GOST, and validators must not trust GOST signatures. Operators should migrate to modern algorithms such as ECDSAP256SHA256 or Ed25519.

sections.title: End of Life for GOST in DNSSEC
sections.content:
DNSSEC signs DNS records to prove they are authentic. RFC 5933 defined two Russian cryptographic standards for this: GOST R 34.10-2001 (a signature algorithm, mnemonic ECC-GOST) and GOST R 34.11-94 (a digest algorithm). These were added in 2010 to support Russian and CIS networks.

However, the Russian standards authority (Rosstandart) officially deprecated both algorithms in August 2012 in favor of newer versions (GOST 2012). GOST ECC-GOST has never seen significant deployment in DNSSEC and was already marked as not recommended.
sections.plainLanguage: An old signing method was added to DNS in 2010, but Russia retired it in 2012. It never really caught on, and everyone moved to better methods.

sections.title: Deprecation and Mandatory Non-Use
sections.content:
RFC 9906 updates the IANA DNS Security Algorithm Numbers registry and the Digest Algorithms registry to mark both algorithms as DEPRECATED. More importantly, it imposes hard requirements:

  • GOST R 34.11-94 MUST NOT be used to create new Delegation Signer (DS) records, and validating resolvers MUST treat DS records using it as insecure.
  • GOST R 34.10-2001 MUST NOT be used to create DNSKEY or RRSIG records, and validators MUST treat such records as unsupported.

These rules prevent reliance on obsolete algorithms while allowing existing records to be treated gracefully (as insecure rather than as validation failures).
sections.plainLanguage: From now on, you must not sign DNS with GOST. If someone gives you a GOST signature, treat it like it's not there and use something else.

sections.title: Migration Path
sections.content: Zone operators currently using ECC-GOST must switch to supported algorithms (such as RSASSA-PKIX or ECDSA). DNS registries should block their customers from uploading GOST DS records. This RFC does not make GOST validation a hard error (which would break zones accidentally signed with GOST), but instead treats GOST as absent, allowing zones with multiple DS records to fall back to other algorithms.
sections.plainLanguage: If your zone uses GOST signatures, change them now to modern algorithms. Registries will stop accepting GOST DS records.
